slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
The tributary valleys of Touraine hide some of the Loire's most intriguing and overlooked red wines. Pineau d'Aunis — the Loire's most distinctively spicy indigenous grape — finds its true home in the Loir (no 'e') Valley north of Tours. Meanwhile, the city of Orléans contributes its own ancient wine tradition with rare Pinot Noir expressions. This lesson explores these northern outposts of Touraine's red wine world.

AOCs Covered in This Lesson

Coteaux du Loir (red), Coteaux du Vendômois (red/rosé), Orléans (red), Orléans-Cléry
slides.1.title: Touraine Tributary Reds
slides.1.content:
🌿 Coteaux du Loir (Rouge)

Located along the Loir river (tributary, flows southwest — not the main Loire), north of Tours. The coolest sub-region in the Loire wine world. Main red grape: Pineau d'Aunis — producing light-bodied reds with extraordinary white-pepper spice, wild strawberry, and floral character. Also Cabernet Franc and Gamay blends. Best enjoyed slightly chilled at 13°C. Rare and collector-sought.

🌶️ Coteaux du Vendômois (Rouge / Rosé)

Further west along the Loir valley. Known especially for its gris (light rosé) style made from Pineau d'Aunis — pale color, pepper, floral, extremely rare. Red wines blend Pineau d'Aunis, Cabernet Franc, and Gamay. Minimal production; one of France's most under-the-radar appellations.

🏙️ Orléans (Rouge) and Orléans-Cléry

Orléans: Red wines from the ancient city of Orléans (historically important for wine trade). Pinot Noir and Meunier blend — light, Burgundy-adjacent style. Also Cabernet Franc. Very small production revived in the 2000s by passionate growers.

Orléans-Cléry: A separate AOC for 100% Cabernet Franc reds — structured, Loire-mineral, elegant. Often compared to a lighter Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which AOC is covered in this lesson?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Coteaux du Loir is one of the Loire's most fascinating and overlooked red wine AOCs — the homeland of Pineau d'Aunis. Its cool climate and unique spicy grape variety produce wines with white-pepper character unlike anything else in France.
